verdict.rationale: Azure's own managed identities let applications obtain Microsoft Entra tokens without managing any credentials, which covers the 'services' half of the no-long-lived-key story. Nothing in the pack documents OIDC or workload identity federation that issues short-lived credentials to external CI systems, and nothing shows end-to-end documentation. Missing for 10: OIDC/workload identity federation for CI pipelines, evidence that issued credentials are short-lived, end-to-end setup documentation, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a security engineer, nothing ships a long-lived key — OIDC/workload identity federation issues short-lived credentials to CI and services, documented end to end

citations.quote: Applications can use managed identities to obtain Microsoft Entra tokens without having to manage any credentials.
